decision: Creators are dispatched like rides: a map with fan-density heat and venues, moving creators, an event panel with a fill bar and ETAs, and a surge badge
why: Event coverage fails on logistics, not ideas; the dispatch pattern shows who is where and who is late at a glance.
value: The event manager sees gaps before the event starts.

decision: The screen replays last night's pop-up on the world clock (one sim second per replay second) and says so, because it is early morning in Seoul at the world's default time
why: Calling a 04:18 KST screen 'live' would be false; a labeled replay keeps motion honest and still responds to Pause, 10× and 60×.
alternative: Fake a live event at the wrong local time.
value: Credible motion that never contradicts the market clocks in the header.

decision: The Seoul map is drawn SVG (river, roads, districts, heat gradients) and creators move by interpolating along polylines
why: The free-tier rules forbid map APIs and tiles; a schematic map is also easier to read than a street map for dispatch.
value: Zero map requests, and the whole screen is a few kilobytes.

decision: The AI suggests re-routing a creator from a quiet backup venue to the densest exit, with its signals, and nothing moves until a person accepts
why: Moving people is a commitment to them; the suggestion saves the analysis, the manager keeps the decision.
value: More coverage where fans are, with a person accountable for each move.

decision: Canceling for weather sends an automatic brief to every assigned creator (paid in full, reschedule vote) and releases them on the board
why: Cancellations are normal; creators who hear first from the product and get paid come back next time.
value: Trust with the creator network survives a canceled event.
